**Kristoffer Kristofferson** (June 22, 1936 – September 28, 2024) was an American musician, songwriter, and actor. He was a pioneering figure in the [outlaw country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outlaw_country "Outlaw country") movement of the 1970s, moving away from the polished [Nashville sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_sound "Nashville sound") and toward a more raw, introspective style. Some of his most famous songs include "[Me and Bobby McGee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Me_and_Bobby_McGee "Me and Bobby McGee")" (1970), "[For the Good Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_the_Good_Times_(song) "For the Good Times (song)")" (1968), "[Sunday Mornin' Comin' Down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunday_Mornin'_Comin'_Down "Sunday Mornin' Comin' Down")" (1969), and "[Help Me Make It Through the Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help_Me_Make_It_Through_the_Night "Help Me Make It Through the Night")" (1970), which were also recorded by and became hits for other artists.

Kristofferson was born in Brownsville, Texas. The family relocated to San Mateo, California, during his childhood. He enlisted in military service during the early 1960s. After one single for [Epic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_Records "Epic Records"), Kristofferson was signed by [Monument Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monument_Records "Monument Records") in 1969. Throughout his career, he recorded a total of 10 albums for Monument, two albums for [Mercury Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_Records "Mercury Records"), one album each for Justice Records and [Atlantic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_Records "Atlantic Records"), and two albums each for New West Records and KK Records.

In 1971, Kristofferson made his film debut in _[The Last Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Last\_Movie "The Last Movie")_ and devoted much of the later decade to making Hollywood films. Some of his most famous films include his collaborations with director [Sam Peckinpah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Peckinpah "Sam Peckinpah") on _[Pat Garrett and Billy the Kid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat\_Garrett\_and\_Billy\_the\_Kid "Pat Garrett and Billy the Kid")_ (1973) and _[Convoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy\_(1978\_film) "Convoy (1978 film)")_ (1978), as well a minor role in _[Bring Me the Head of Alfredo Garcia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bring\_Me\_the\_Head\_of\_Alfredo\_Garcia "Bring Me the Head of Alfredo Garcia")_ (1974). Other roles of his include _[Cisco Pike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cisco\_Pike "Cisco Pike")_ (1972), _[A Star Is Born](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Star\_Is\_Born\_(1976\_film) "A Star Is Born (1976 film)")_ (1976), _[Heaven's Gate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heaven's\_Gate\_(film) "Heaven's Gate (film)")_ (1980) and the [_Blade_ film trilogy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blade_(franchise) "Blade (franchise)") (1998–2004)

Kristofferson was also a member of the [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") supergroup [the Highwaymen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Highwaymen "The Highwaymen") between 1985 and 1995. He has charted 12 times on the American _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")_[Hot Country Songs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Country_Songs "Hot Country Songs") charts; his highest-peaking singles there are "Why Me" and "Highwayman", which reached number one in 1973 and 1985, respectively. He was inducted into the [Country Music Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_Music_Hall_of_Fame_and_Museum "Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum") in 2004 and received the [Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Lifetime_Achievement_Award "Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award") in 2014. He was a three-time [Grammy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards") winner, out of 13 total nominations.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-1) Kristofferson died in 2024 at the age of 88, three years after announcing his retirement.

### 1936–1965: Early life and military service

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kris_Kristofferson&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: 1936–1965: Early life and military service")]

Kristoffer Kristofferson was born in [Brownsville, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brownsville,_Texas "Brownsville, Texas"), the oldest of three children born to Mary Ann (née Ashbrook) and Henry Kristofferson, a [United States Army Air Corps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Air_Corps "United States Army Air Corps") officer (later a [major general](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_general "Major general") in the [United States Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Force "United States Air Force")).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-Times,_San_Mateo-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-PCM-3) Henry later worked as a manager for [Saudi Aramco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_Aramco "Saudi Aramco") after retiring from the Air Force.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-AllMusicBio-4) During Kristofferson's childhood, his father encouraged him to pursue a military career.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-Outlaw-5)

Kristofferson moved around frequently as a youth because of his father's military service, and the family settled in [San Mateo, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Mateo,_California "San Mateo, California").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-Zompolis-2004-6) He attended [San Mateo High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Mateo_High_School "San Mateo High School"), where he graduated in 1954. At age 17, Kristofferson took a summer job with a [dredging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dredging "Dredging") contractor on [Wake Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Island "Wake Island") in the western Pacific Ocean.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-7)

Kristofferson went to [Pomona College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pomona_College "Pomona College") in Claremont, California, as a literature major. He studied under [Frederick Sontag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_Sontag "Frederick Sontag"), whom he considered an important influence in his life.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-PCM-3) His early writing included prize-winning essays that were published in _[The Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Atlantic "The Atlantic")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-8) During this time, Kristofferson worked in various construction jobs and as a firefighter.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-PCM-3) He appeared in the March 31, 1958, issue of _[Sports Illustrated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports\_Illustrated "Sports Illustrated")_ for his achievements in collegiate [rugby union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rugby_union "Rugby union"), [American football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football"), and track and field.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-9) He and his classmates also revived the [Claremont Colleges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claremont_Colleges "Claremont Colleges") Rugby Club, and it remains a Southern California rugby institution. Kristofferson graduated in 1958, earning a [Bachelor of Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Arts "Bachelor of Arts") degree, _[summa cum laude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin\_honors#Distinctions "Latin honors")_, in [English Literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_Literature "English Literature"). He was elected to the [Phi Beta Kappa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phi_Beta_Kappa "Phi Beta Kappa") society his junior year.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-PCM-3)

Also in 1958, Kristofferson was awarded a [Rhodes Scholarship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhodes_Scholarship "Rhodes Scholarship") to the [University of Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Oxford "University of Oxford") in Oxford, England,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-10) studying at [Merton College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merton_College,_Oxford "Merton College, Oxford").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-MCreg-11) While performing his own songs there, Kristofferson signed with [Larry Parnes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Parnes "Larry Parnes"), best known for his work with [Tommy Steele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Steele "Tommy Steele"). Parnes was working to sell Kristofferson as "a Yank at Oxford" to the British public; Kristofferson was willing to accept that promotional approach if it helped his singing career, which he hoped would enable him to progress toward his goal of becoming a novelist.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-turns80-12)

In early 1959, Kristofferson signed a recording contract with Paul Lincoln's Top Rank label as "Kris Carson", but these recordings were unsuccessful.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-AllMusicBio-4)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-14) In 1960, Kristofferson graduated with a [B.Phil.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/B.Phil. "B.Phil.") in [English literature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_literature "English literature").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-PCM-3)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-MCreg-11)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-16)

In 1961, he married his longtime girlfriend, Frances "Fran" Mavia Beer.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-MCreg-11)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-17) Also in 1961, Kristofferson joined the [United States Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army "United States Army") and was commissioned as a [second lieutenant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_lieutenant "Second lieutenant"). He attended [U.S. Army Ranger School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Army_Ranger_School "U.S. Army Ranger School") and completed helicopter pilot training at [Fort Rucker, Alabama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Rucker,_Alabama "Fort Rucker, Alabama").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-18) He relocated Beer and their newborn daughter to [West Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Germany "West Germany"), where he served as a member of the [8th Infantry Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/8th_Infantry_Division_(United_States) "8th Infantry Division (United States)").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-AllMusicBio-4)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-19) During this period, Kristofferson was promoted to the rank of [captain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_(United_States_O-3) "Captain (United States O-3)") and resumed his music career, forming a band to play at service clubs. It was at this point that he met [Marijohn Wilkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marijohn_Wilkin "Marijohn Wilkin"), the aunt of his platoon commander.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-AllMusicBio-4) In 1965, after his tour in West Germany ended, Kristofferson was re-assigned to teach English literature at the [United States Military Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Military_Academy "United States Military Academy") in West Point, New York.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-21)

### 1965–1972: Early music and film career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kris_Kristofferson&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1965–1972: Early music and film career")]

In June 1965, while on a two-week leave from his assignments, Kristofferson contacted Wilkin in Nashville, Tennessee, and decided to become a country music songwriter. He resigned from the Army and relocated his family to Nashville that year, exacerbating his relationship with his parents.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-24) Wilkin signed Kristofferson to her publishing house Buckhorn Music and pitched his song "Talkin' Vietnam Blues" to singer [Dave Dudley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Dudley "Dave Dudley"). Concurrently, Kristofferson held various jobs including as a bartender, a construction worker, and a railroad worker. He later worked as a janitor for [Columbia Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Records "Columbia Records"), which afforded him the possibility of talking directly with the artists and a presence during recording sessions.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHurd,_Mary201522%E2%80%9323-25) He released his debut single containing his songs "Golden Idol" and "Killing Time" in 1967 on [Epic Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epic_Records "Epic Records").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-AllMusicBio-4)

After his second child was born with esophagus issues in 1968, Kristofferson worked at [Petroleum Helicopters International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petroleum_Helicopters_International "Petroleum Helicopters International") (PHI) in [Lafayette, Louisiana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lafayette,_Louisiana "Lafayette, Louisiana"). While flying workers to and from oil rigs in the [Gulf of Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_Mexico "Gulf of Mexico"), he would often write new songs. At weekends, he returned to Nashville, and for the following week he would pitch the songs around town before returning to Louisiana.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEThibodeaux,_Ron2006-26) The trips exhausted Kristofferson; his children were living with Fran in California and he felt his career as a songwriter was failing. PHI also admonished him for his increased alcohol consumption. Upon returning to Nashville the same week,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHurd,_Mary201523-27) Kristofferson learned three of his songs had been recorded: "Jody and the Kid" by [Roy Drusky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Drusky "Roy Drusky"), "[Help Me Make It Through the Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help_Me_Make_It_Through_the_Night "Help Me Make It Through the Night")" by [Jerry Lee Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Lee_Lewis "Jerry Lee Lewis") and "[Me and Bobby McGee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Me_and_Bobby_McGee "Me and Bobby McGee")" by [Roger Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Miller "Roger Miller").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-FOOTNOTELarkin200628-28)

Through [June Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/June_Carter "June Carter"), Kristofferson first attempted to pitch material to her husband [Johnny Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Cash "Johnny Cash"). Carter took the demos, which were eventually lost in a pile of other material Cash had received.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEEdmondson,_Jacqueline2013631-29) At the time, Kristofferson worked on the weekends for the [Tennessee National Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tennessee_Military_Department "Tennessee Military Department"). To attract Cash's attention, Kristofferson landed a helicopter on Cash's property.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHurd,_Mary201526-30) Cash eventually invited Kristofferson to a "guitar pull" party in his house. Cash was impressed and invited Kristofferson to perform with him at the 1969 [Newport Folk Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newport_Folk_Festival "Newport Folk Festival").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHurd,_Mary201527-31) Unsatisfied by Buckhorn Music, Kristofferson decided to change labels. [Monument Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monument_Records "Monument Records") director [Bob Beckham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Beckham "Bob Beckham") invited Kristofferson to play songs for him and label owner [Fred Foster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Foster "Fred Foster").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHurd,_Mary201527-31) Kristofferson performed "To Beat the Devil", "Jody and the Kid", "The Best of All Possible Worlds" and "Duvalier's Dream"; Foster was impressed and signed Kristofferson to Monument as a recording artist and [Combine Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combine_Music "Combine Music") as a songwriter. The ten-year contract required Kristofferson to submit ten records containing songs he had written.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHurd,_Mary201528-32) Kristofferson was surprised he had been signed as a singer; he told Foster at the time: "I can't sing, I sound like a frog!"[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHurd,_Mary201528-32) Kristofferson later said Buckhorn Music had not allowed him to record demos of his compositions.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEThomson,_Graeme2016-33)

In 1969, Kristofferson divorced Beer and left Nashville to join the production of his first motion picture, [Dennis Hopper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dennis_Hopper "Dennis Hopper")'s _[The Last Movie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Last\_Movie "The Last Movie")_, in Peru. In his absence, Cash continued promoting Kristofferson's original songs with other singers. Upon returning to Nashville, Kristofferson learned of his new popularity and started to work on his debut album for Monument, _[Kristofferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kristofferson\_(album) "Kristofferson (album)")_.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHurst,_Jack19703-5-34) As his manager and producer, Foster had decided to keep some of Kristofferson's original material from being passed to other artists. The new material, as well as his songs that had already been recorded by other artists, were included in the recording sessions, which were held at [Monument Recording Studio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Foster_Sound_Studio "Fred Foster Sound Studio").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMiller,_Stephen2009129-35)

Monument released _Kristofferson_ in June 1970. Kristofferson wrote or co-wrote every song on the album. He collaborated with Marijohn's son, [John Buck Wilkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Buck_Wilkin "John Buck Wilkin"), on "Blame it on the Stones". Though _Kristofferson_ was not a commercial success, it received positive reviews from critics. According to [Robert Hilburn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Hilburn "Robert Hilburn") of the _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_Angeles\_Times "Los Angeles Times")_, the album "is able to combine lyric sophistication with country music's traditional interest in everyday problems".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-36) The commercial success of "Sunday Mornin' Comin' Down" led to the first of several industry awards nominations for the singer. Johnny Cash's rendition of the single earned Kristofferson his first [Country Music Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_Music_Association "Country Music Association") award for [Song of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_Music_Association_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "Country Music Association Award for Song of the Year") that November.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-37)

Also in 1970, he made his debut performance as a singer at the Los Angeles nightclub [The Troubadour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troubadour_(West_Hollywood,_California) "Troubadour (West Hollywood, California)"). [Fred Roos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fred_Roos "Fred Roos"), the casting director of [Bob Rafelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Rafelson "Bob Rafelson")'s _[Five Easy Pieces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Five\_Easy\_Pieces "Five Easy Pieces")_, invited him to audition for his film debut for a leading role on _[Two-Lane Blacktop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-Lane\_Blacktop "Two-Lane Blacktop")_. Kristofferson, who was signed to [Columbia Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Records "Columbia Records"), arrived to the appointment intoxicated and left. Kristofferson was next offered [Bill L. Norton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_L._Norton "Bill L. Norton")'s script for _[Cisco Pike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cisco\_Pike "Cisco Pike")_ by Columbia. His peers encouraged him to reject the role and to take acting lessons instead, but he accepted the part, and later said; "I read the script and I could identify with this cat" and that acting is "understanding a character, and then being just as honest as you can possibly be".[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBurke1974-38)

Kristofferson began an 18-month tour, during which he suffered a bout of [walking pneumonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atypical_pneumonia "Atypical pneumonia"), which was worsened by his alcohol consumption. While performing, he would not face the audience and mumbled the words to his songs. Eventually, he was hospitalized.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHurd,_Mary201542-39) During the tour, Kristofferson performed on _[The Johnny Cash Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Johnny\_Cash\_Show\_(TV\_series) "The Johnny Cash Show (TV series)")_. While in California, Kristofferson befriended singer [Janis Joplin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janis_Joplin "Janis Joplin").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStreissguth,_Michael201387-40) Upon returning to Nashville in early 1971, he received with his mail at Combine Music Joplin's posthumous album _[Pearl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl\_(Janis\_Joplin\_album) "Pearl (Janis Joplin album)")_, which at the time was still unreleased. Joplin's album included a cover of his original composition "[Me and Bobby McGee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Me_and_Bobby_McGee "Me and Bobby McGee")". The following morning, he returned to the studio and recorded his second Monument album, _[The Silver Tongued Devil and I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Silver\_Tongued\_Devil\_and\_I "The Silver Tongued Devil and I")_, which was released that July.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-FOOTNOTEStreissguth,_Michael201388,_89-41) He wrote nine of the album's 10 songs, including the single "[Lovin' Her Was Easier (than Anything I'll Ever Do Again)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lovin'_Her_Was_Easier_(than_Anything_I'll_Ever_Do_Again) "Lovin' Her Was Easier (than Anything I'll Ever Do Again)")". He collaborated with songwriter [Shel Silverstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shel_Silverstein "Shel Silverstein") on "The Taker" and keyboardist [Donnie Fritts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donnie_Fritts "Donnie Fritts") on "Epitaph (Black and Blue)". Also included on the album was a cover of [Bobby Bare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Bare "Bobby Bare")'s "Good Christian Soldier". "Lovin' Her Was Easier (than Anything I'll Ever Do Again)" reached number 46 on _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")_[Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") and number 4 on [Adult Contemporary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adult_Contemporary_(chart) "Adult Contemporary (chart)"). These songs would later be used on the soundtrack for _Cisco Pike_, which was released on January 14, 1972.

[![Image 2](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/be/Kris_Kristofferson_Rita_Coolidge.jpg/250px-Kris_Kristofferson_Rita_Coolidge.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kris_Kristofferson_Rita_Coolidge.jpg)

Kristofferson with Rita Coolidge at the 1972 [Dripping Springs Reunion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson's_Fourth_of_July_Picnic#Dripping_Springs_Reunion "Willie Nelson's Fourth of July Picnic")

That February, Monument released his third album _[Border Lord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Border\_Lord "Border Lord")_. The album was all-new material and sales were sluggish. He also swept the [Grammy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards") that year with numerous songs nominated, winning country song of the year for "Help Me Make It Through the Night". Kristofferson's fourth album, _[Jesus Was a Capricorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesus\_Was\_a\_Capricorn "Jesus Was a Capricorn")_, initially had slow sales, but the third single, "[Why Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Why_Me_(Kris_Kristofferson_song) "Why Me (Kris Kristofferson song)")", was a success and significantly increased album sales. It sold over one million copies, and was awarded a [gold disc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_recording_certification "Music recording certification") by the [RIAA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RIAA "RIAA") on November 8, 1973.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-The_Book_of_Golden_Discs-42) Kristofferson appeared with Rita Coolidge on the BBC television series _[The Old Grey Whistle Test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Old\_Grey\_Whistle\_Test "The Old Grey Whistle Test")_, performing "Help Me Make It Through the Night". [Al Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Green "Al Green") later released his version of "[For the Good Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/For_the_Good_Times_(song) "For the Good Times (song)")" on the album _[I'm Still in Love with You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I'm\_Still\_in\_Love\_with\_You\_(Al\_Green\_album) "I'm Still in Love with You (Al Green album)")_.

### 1973–1985: Commercial peak

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kris_Kristofferson&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 1973–1985: Commercial peak")]

In April 1973, Kristofferson received an honorary doctorate in fine arts from Pomona College during Alumni Weekend, accompanied by Cash and Coolidge.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-43) Four months later, Kristofferson married Coolidge. The duo released an album titled _[Full Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Full\_Moon\_(Kris\_Kristofferson\_and\_Rita\_Coolidge\_album) "Full Moon (Kris Kristofferson and Rita Coolidge album)")_, another success buoyed by numerous hit singles and Grammy nominations.

His fifth album, _[Spooky Lady's Sideshow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spooky\_Lady's\_Sideshow "Spooky Lady's Sideshow")_, released in 1974, was a commercial failure. Artists such as [Ronnie Milsap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_Milsap "Ronnie Milsap"), [Willie Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson "Willie Nelson") and [Johnny Duncan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Duncan_(country_singer) "Johnny Duncan (country singer)") continued to record Kristofferson's material with success, but his rough vocal style and anti-pop sound kept his own audience to a minimum.

In March 1979, Kristofferson participated in the [Havana Jam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Havana_Jam "Havana Jam") festival in [Havana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Havana "Havana") alongside several notable American and Cuban artists. His performance is captured on Ernesto Juan Castellanos's documentary _Havana Jam '79_.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-44) That November, Kristofferson and Coolidge appeared on _[The Muppet Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Muppet\_Show "The Muppet Show")_, where Kristofferson sang "[Help Me Make It Through the Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help_Me_Make_It_Through_the_Night "Help Me Make It Through the Night")" with [Miss Piggy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miss_Piggy "Miss Piggy"), Coolidge sang "[We're All Alone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We're_All_Alone "We're All Alone")" with forest animals, and the pair sang "[Song I'd Like to Sing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Full_Moon_(Kris_Kristofferson_and_Rita_Coolidge_album) "Full Moon (Kris Kristofferson and Rita Coolidge album)")" with the Muppet monsters. They divorced in 1980.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-45)

In 1982, Kristofferson joined [Willie Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson "Willie Nelson"), [Dolly Parton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolly_Parton "Dolly Parton"), and [Brenda Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brenda_Lee "Brenda Lee") on _[The Winning Hand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Winning\_Hand "The Winning Hand")_, a double album consisting of remastered and updated performances of recordings the four artists had made for the Monument label during the mid-1960s; the album reached the top ten on the U.S. country album charts. He married again, to Lisa Meyers, and concentrated on films for a time, appearing in the 1984 releases _[The Lost Honor of Kathryn Beck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lost\_Honor\_of\_Kathryn\_Beck "The Lost Honor of Kathryn Beck")_, _[Flashpoint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flashpoint\_(1984\_film) "Flashpoint (1984 film)")_, and _[Songwriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songwriter\_(film) "Songwriter (film)")_. Nelson and Kristofferson both appeared in _Songwriter_, and Kristofferson was nominated for an [Academy Award for Best Original Score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Original_Score "Academy Award for Best Original Score"). The album _[Music from Songwriter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music\_from\_Songwriter "Music from Songwriter")_, featuring Nelson-Kristofferson duets, was a country success.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-turns80-12)

For the next several years, Kristofferson focused on acting. He appeared in _[Cisco Pike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cisco\_Pike "Cisco Pike")_ (1972) with [Gene Hackman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_Hackman "Gene Hackman"); _[Blume in Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blume\_in\_Love "Blume in Love")_ (1973), directed by [Paul Mazursky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Mazursky "Paul Mazursky"); three [Sam Peckinpah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Peckinpah "Sam Peckinpah") films: _[Pat Garrett and Billy the Kid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat\_Garrett\_and\_Billy\_the\_Kid "Pat Garrett and Billy the Kid")_ (1973), _[Bring Me the Head of Alfredo Garcia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bring\_Me\_the\_Head\_of\_Alfredo\_Garcia "Bring Me the Head of Alfredo Garcia")_ (1974), and _[Convoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy\_(1978\_film) "Convoy (1978 film)")_ (1978); and [Michael Ritchie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Ritchie_(filmmaker) "Michael Ritchie (filmmaker)")'s _[Semi-Tough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-Tough "Semi-Tough")_ (1977) with [Burt Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burt_Reynolds "Burt Reynolds"). He continued acting in [Martin Scorsese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Scorsese "Martin Scorsese")'s _[Alice Doesn't Live Here Anymore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice\_Doesn't\_Live\_Here\_Anymore "Alice Doesn't Live Here Anymore")_ (1974), _[Vigilante Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vigilante\_Force "Vigilante Force")_ (1976), _[The Sailor Who Fell from Grace with the Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sailor\_Who\_Fell\_from\_Grace\_with\_the\_Sea\_(film) "The Sailor Who Fell from Grace with the Sea (film)")_ (1976), and the romantic drama _[A Star Is Born](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Star\_Is\_Born\_(1976\_film) "A Star Is Born (1976 film)")_ (1976) with [Barbra Streisand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbra_Streisand "Barbra Streisand"), for which he received a [Golden Globe Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Motion_Picture_%E2%80%93_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy"). At the peak of his box office power, Kristofferson turned down [William Friedkin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Friedkin "William Friedkin")'s _[Sorcerer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sorcerer\_(film) "Sorcerer (film)")_ (1977) and the romantic war film _[Hanover Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanover\_Street\_(film) "Hanover Street (film)")_ (1979). Despite his success with Streisand, Kristofferson's solo musical career headed downward with his non-charting ninth album, _[Shake Hands with the Devil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shake\_Hands\_with\_the\_Devil\_(album) "Shake Hands with the Devil (album)")_. His next film, the two-part 1979 [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC")-TV movie _[Freedom Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freedom\_Road "Freedom Road")_, did not get good ratings.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Kristofferson was next cast in the lead role as the enigmatic Sheriff James Averill in [Michael Cimino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Cimino "Michael Cimino")'s bleak and sprawling 1980 anti-Western _[Heaven's Gate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heaven's\_Gate\_(film) "Heaven's Gate (film)")_. Despite being a scandalous studio-bankrupting and industry-changing failure at the time (it cost Kristofferson his Hollywood A-list status), the film gained critical recognition in subsequent years. In 1981, he co-starred with [Jane Fonda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jane_Fonda "Jane Fonda") in _[Rollover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rollover\_(film) "Rollover (film)")_, directed by [Alan J. Pakula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_J._Pakula "Alan J. Pakula"). In 1986, he starred in _[The Last Days of Frank and Jesse James](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Last\_Days\_of\_Frank\_and\_Jesse\_James "The Last Days of Frank and Jesse James")_ with Johnny Cash and [_Flashpoint_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flashpoint_(1984_film) "Flashpoint (1984 film)") with [Treat Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treat_Williams "Treat Williams") in 1984, directed by William Tannen. This was followed, in 1985, by the [neo-noir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neo-noir "Neo-noir") thriller _[Trouble In Mind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trouble\_in\_Mind\_(film) "Trouble in Mind (film)")_ co-starring [Keith Carradine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Carradine "Keith Carradine") and [Lori Singer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lori_Singer "Lori Singer"). In 1987, Kristofferson starred in the seven-episode TV series _[Amerika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amerika\_(miniseries) "Amerika (miniseries)")_ with [Robert Urich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich "Robert Urich") and [Christine Lahti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christine_Lahti "Christine Lahti"). In 1989, he was the male lead in the film _[Millennium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millennium\_(film) "Millennium (film)")_ with [Cheryl Ladd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheryl_Ladd "Cheryl Ladd").

### 1985–2021: Highwaymen and later years

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kris_Kristofferson&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 1985–2021: Highwaymen and later years")]

Nelson and Kristofferson continued their partnership, and by 1985, they added [Waylon Jennings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waylon_Jennings "Waylon Jennings") and [Johnny Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Cash "Johnny Cash") to form the [supergroup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supergroup_(music) "Supergroup (music)")[the Highwaymen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Highwaymen_(country_supergroup) "The Highwaymen (country supergroup)"). Their [self-titled first album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highwayman_(The_Highwaymen_album) "Highwayman (The Highwaymen album)"), released on May 6, was a success, and the supergroup continued working together for a time. The single from the album, a cover of [Jimmy Webb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Webb "Jimmy Webb")'s "[Highwayman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highwayman_(song) "Highwayman (song)")", was awarded the ACM's single of the year in 1985.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-46) In 1985, Kristofferson starred in _[Trouble in Mind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trouble\_in\_Mind\_(film) "Trouble in Mind (film)")_ and released _[Repossessed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Repossessed\_(album) "Repossessed (album)")_, a politically aware album that was a country success, particularly "They Killed Him" (also performed by [Bob Dylan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dylan "Bob Dylan")), a tribute to his heroes, including [Martin Luther King Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Luther_King_Jr. "Martin Luther King Jr."), Jesus, and [Mahatma Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahatma_Gandhi "Mahatma Gandhi").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-47) Kristofferson also appeared in _[Amerika](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amerika\_(miniseries) "Amerika (miniseries)")_ at about the same time, a miniseries that attempted to depict life in America under [Soviet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") control.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-48)

[![Image 3](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/Kris_Kristofferson_SXSW_2006_crop.jpg/250px-Kris_Kristofferson_SXSW_2006_crop.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kris_Kristofferson_SXSW_2006_crop.jpg)

Kristofferson at the 2006 [South by Southwest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_by_Southwest "South by Southwest") Festival

In spite of the success of _[Highwayman 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Highwayman\_2 "Highwayman 2")_ in 1990, Kristofferson's solo recording career slipped significantly in the early 1990s, though he continued to record successfully with the Highwaymen. _[Lone Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lone\_Star\_(1996\_film) "Lone Star (1996 film)")_ (1996 film by [John Sayles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Sayles "John Sayles")) reinvigorated Kristofferson's acting career, and he soon appeared in _[Blade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blade\_(1998\_film) "Blade (1998 film)")_, _[Blade II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blade\_II "Blade II")_, _[Blade: Trinity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blade:\_Trinity "Blade: Trinity")_, _[A Soldier's Daughter Never Cries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Soldier's\_Daughter\_Never\_Cries\_(film) "A Soldier's Daughter Never Cries (film)")_, _[Fire Down Below](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fire\_Down\_Below\_(1997\_film) "Fire Down Below (1997 film)")_, [Tim Burton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Burton "Tim Burton")'s remake of _[Planet of the Apes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Planet\_of\_the\_Apes\_(2001\_film) "Planet of the Apes (2001 film)")_, _[Chelsea Walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea\_Walls "Chelsea Walls")_, _[Payback](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Payback\_(1999\_film) "Payback (1999 film)")_, _[The Jacket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Jacket "The Jacket")_, and _[Fast Food Nation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast\_Food\_Nation\_(film) "Fast Food Nation (film)")_.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-49)

The [Songwriters Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songwriters_Hall_of_Fame "Songwriters Hall of Fame") inducted Kristofferson in 1985, as had the [Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_Songwriters_Hall_of_Fame "Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame") earlier, in 1977. In 1999, _[The Austin Sessions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Austin\_Sessions\_(Kris\_Kristofferson\_album) "The Austin Sessions (Kris Kristofferson album)")_ was released, an album on which Kristofferson reworked some of his favorite songs with the help of artists such as [Mark Knopfler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Knopfler "Mark Knopfler"), [Steve Earle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Earle "Steve Earle"), and [Jackson Browne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Browne "Jackson Browne"). He underwent [coronary artery bypass surgery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronary_artery_bypass_surgery "Coronary artery bypass surgery") shortly after the album's release.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-Outlaw-5)

In 1997, Kristofferson co-starred in the film _[Fire Down Below](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fire\_Down\_Below\_(1997\_film) "Fire Down Below (1997 film)")_ with [Steven Seagal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Seagal "Steven Seagal").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-51) Kristofferson appeared in the [Stephen Norrington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Norrington "Stephen Norrington") film _[Blade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blade\_(1998\_film) "Blade (1998 film)")_, alongside [Wesley Snipes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wesley_Snipes "Wesley Snipes"), as [Blade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blade_(character) "Blade (character)")'s mentor [Abraham Whistler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Whistler "Abraham Whistler"). He reprised the role in _[Blade II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blade\_II "Blade II")_ (2002) and again in _[Blade: Trinity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blade:\_Trinity "Blade: Trinity")_ (2004). In 1998 he starred in _[Dance with Me](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dance\_with\_Me\_(1998\_film) "Dance with Me (1998 film)")_ along with [Vanessa Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanessa_Williams "Vanessa Williams") and [Chayanne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chayanne "Chayanne").

In 2003, _[Broken Freedom Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broken\_Freedom\_Song:\_Live\_from\_San\_Francisco "Broken Freedom Song: Live from San Francisco")_ was released, a live album recorded in San Francisco. That year, he received the "Spirit of Americana" free speech award from the [Americana Music Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americana_Music_Association "Americana Music Association").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-52) In 2004, he began experiencing memory problems which lasted for the next 11 years.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-WashPostObituary-53) That November, he was inducted into the [Country Music Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_Music_Hall_of_Fame "Country Music Hall of Fame").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-54)

On October 21, 2005, the film _[Dreamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dreamer\_(2005\_film) "Dreamer (2005 film)")_ was released, in which Kristofferson played the role of "Pop", a retired thoroughbred horse trainer. The film was inspired by the true story of the mare [Mariah's Storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariah's_Storm "Mariah's Storm") which won the Turfway Breeders Cup Classic. In 2006, he received the [Johnny Mercer Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Mercer_Award "Johnny Mercer Award") from the [Songwriters Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Songwriters_Hall_of_Fame "Songwriters Hall of Fame") and released his first album full of new material in 11 years; _[This Old Road](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This\_Old\_Road "This Old Road")_. Also in 2006, Kristofferson starred with [Geneviève Bujold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genevi%C3%A8ve_Bujold "Geneviève Bujold") in the film _[Disappearances](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disappearances\_(film) "Disappearances (film)")_ about whiskey running from [Quebec](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quebec "Quebec") to the U.S. during the [Great Depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression "Great Depression").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-55)

On April 21, 2007, Kristofferson won [CMT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CMT_(American_TV_channel) "CMT (American TV channel)")'s Johnny Cash Visionary Award. [Rosanne Cash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosanne_Cash "Rosanne Cash"), Cash's daughter, presented the honor during the April 16 awards show in Nashville. Previous recipients include Cash, [Hank Williams Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hank_Williams_Jr. "Hank Williams Jr."), [Loretta Lynn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loretta_Lynn "Loretta Lynn"), [Reba McEntire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reba_McEntire "Reba McEntire"), and the [Dixie Chicks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Chicks "The Chicks"). "John was my hero before he was my friend, and anything with his name on it is really an honor in my eyes," Kristofferson said during a phone interview. "I was thinking back to when I first met him, and if I ever thought that I'd be getting an award with his name on it, it would have carried me through a lot of hard times."[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-56)

Kristofferson's next studio album, titled _[Closer to the Bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Closer\_to\_the\_Bone "Closer to the Bone")_, was released in September 2009. It is produced by [Don Was](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Was "Don Was") on the [New West Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_West_Records "New West Records") label. Before the release, Kristofferson remarked: "I like the intimacy of the new album. It has a general mood of reflecting on where we all are at this time of life."[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-Kris_Kristofferson-57) That November, Kristofferson was honored as a [BMI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadcast_Music,_Inc. "Broadcast Music, Inc.") Icon at the 57th annual BMI Country Awards. Throughout his career, Kristofferson's songwriting garnered 48 BMI Country and Pop Awards.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-58) He later remarked, "The great thing about being a songwriter is you can hear your baby interpreted by so many people that have creative talents vocally that I don't have."[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-cnnnov112009-59) Kristofferson had always denied having a good voice, and had said that as he had aged, any quality it once had was beginning to decay.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-60)

### 2021–2024: Retirement

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kris_Kristofferson&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2021–2024: Retirement")]

By January 2021, Kristofferson announced his retirement from performing, citing age and concerns regarding the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-72) Kristofferson's final performance was held in Los Angeles at the [Hollywood Bowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Bowl "Hollywood Bowl") on April 29, 2023, where he sang a cover of "Lovin' You Was Easier" with Rosanne Cash in honor of Willie Nelson's 90th birthday;[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-Maui-73) the concert was later released as _Long Story Short: Willie Nelson 90_ that December.

In 1961, Kristofferson married his longtime girlfriend Frances "Fran" Mavia Beer, but they divorced in 1969.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-MCreg-11)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-Campbell-2020-74)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-75) Kristofferson briefly dated [Janis Joplin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janis_Joplin "Janis Joplin") before her death in October 1970.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-Campbell-2020-74) His second marriage was to singer [Rita Coolidge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Coolidge "Rita Coolidge") in 1973, ending in divorce in 1980.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-Zompolis-2004-6)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-Campbell-2020-74) Kristofferson married Lisa Meyers in 1983.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-Campbell-2020-74)

Kristofferson and Meyers owned a home in Las Flores Canyon in [Malibu, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malibu,_California "Malibu, California"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-Outlaw-5) and they also resided in [Hana, Hawaii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hana,_Hawaii "Hana, Hawaii") from 1990 until his death.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-Campbell-2020-74) Kristofferson had eight children from his three marriages: two from his first marriage, one from his second marriage, and five from his third marriage.

Kristofferson also had relationships outside of his marriages and fully embraced the "drugs, rocknroll life-style, leaving different sets of women to raise all eight of his kids."[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-76)[_[failed verification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_]

### Political views and advocacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kris_Kristofferson&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Political views and advocacy")]

Kristofferson was a vocal opponent of the [Gulf War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_War "Gulf War") and [Iraq War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iraq_War "Iraq War") and a critic of a number of United States military interventions and foreign policy positions, including the [United States invasion of Panama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_invasion_of_Panama "United States invasion of Panama") and U.S. support of the [Contras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Contras "Contras") during the [Nicaraguan Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicaraguan_Revolution "Nicaraguan Revolution") .[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-77)

Kristofferson endorsed [Jesse Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_Jackson "Jesse Jackson")'s [presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jesse_Jackson_1988_presidential_campaign "Jesse Jackson 1988 presidential campaign") in 1988 and [Ross Perot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ross_Perot "Ross Perot")'s [presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ross_Perot_1992_presidential_campaign "Ross Perot 1992 presidential campaign") in 1992.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-78)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-79)

Kristofferson's debut studio album included a pro–[Vietnam War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vietnam_War "Vietnam War") song, but he said that he later became an opponent of the war after speaking with returning soldiers who had seen combat. Speaking about a soldier who had told him that he had witnessed other soldiers throwing people out of helicopters during interrogation, Kristofferson said, "The notion that you could make a young person do something so inhumane to another soldier—or even worse, a civilian—convinced me that we were in the wrong." Kristofferson called himself a "dove with claws" and remained proud of his military service in spite of his anti-war views.

In a 1991 interview on New Zealand TV, he condemned media support for the Gulf War, saying "The lapdog media cranks out propaganda that would make a [Nazi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nazi "Nazi") blush."[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-80) Kristofferson was a supporter of the [United Farm Workers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Farm_Workers "United Farm Workers") and appeared at several rallies and benefits for them, campaigning with [Cesar Chavez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cesar_Chavez "Cesar Chavez") for the passage of Proposition 14. He continued to play at benefits for the UFW through the 2010s. In 1987, he played at a benefit concert for [Leonard Peltier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonard_Peltier "Leonard Peltier") with [Jackson Browne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Browne "Jackson Browne"), [Willie Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson "Willie Nelson") and [Joni Mitchell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joni_Mitchell "Joni Mitchell"). In 1995, he dedicated a song to [Mumia Abu-Jamal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumia_Abu-Jamal "Mumia Abu-Jamal") at a concert in Philadelphia, and was booed by the crowd.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-81)

He performed in benefit concerts for [Palestinian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinians "Palestinians") children, and said that he "found a considerable lack of work as a result."[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-82) At a [Bob Dylan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Dylan "Bob Dylan") anniversary concert shortly after [Sinéad O'Connor's protest on _Saturday Night Live_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sin%C3%A9ad_O'Connor_on_Saturday_Night_Live "Sinéad O'Connor on Saturday Night Live") in 1992, he showed solidarity with her when she was booed by the crowd.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-83)

Kristofferson died in his Hana, Hawaii, home on September 28, 2024, at the age of 88. His family did not provide a cause of death.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-84)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-85) He had requested for the first three lines of [Leonard Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leonard_Cohen "Leonard Cohen")'s "[Bird on the Wire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird_on_the_Wire "Bird on the Wire")" on his tombstone:[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-86)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-87)

> Like a bird on the wire
> 
>  Like a drunk in a midnight choir
> 
>  I have tried in my way to be free

Family and associates, including [Dolly Parton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolly_Parton "Dolly Parton"), [Reba McEntire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reba_McEntire "Reba McEntire") and [Miranda Lambert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert "Miranda Lambert"), paid tribute to Kristofferson on social media,[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-88) while media outlets also published tributes written by singers [Willie Nelson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willie_Nelson "Willie Nelson") and [Ashley McBryde](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashley_McBryde "Ashley McBryde").[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-89)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-90) Many other musicians, artists, and celebrities offered public acknowledgments.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson#cite_note-91)

source_reported.title: Kris Kristofferson

content:
The singer-songwriter and actor Kris Kristofferson has died at the age of 88. He is considered to be one of the great exponents of Country music, but not in the generally accepted style of the Nashville sound, but producing a more edgy, raw kind of so-called ‘outlaw’ music. His own songs are very unlike what we recognise as Country music, with its rowdy, high-spirited rollicking style, because he wrote in a more contemplative way that usually went straight to the heart. As well as being a soloist, he joined forces with other Country singers Willie Nelson, Johnny Cash and Waylon Jennings and they became known as The Highwaymen, a supergroup of outlaw Country musicians.

He was born Kristoffer Kristofferson in Brownsville, Texas, to Lars Henry Kristofferson, a US Army Air Corps officer, and his wife Mary Ann Ashbrook. His father wanted him to have a military career but as the family moved a lot during his father’s time in the service, they ended up in San Mateo, California, where Kris graduated from high school. From 1954 he enrolled at Pomona College with the intention of being a writer. Some of his early and quite personal writings were published in _Atlantic Monthly_. In college he was a fine sportsman, playing rugby union and American football and he excelled in athletics. For his rugby prowess he was featured in _Sports Illustrated_ and graduated with a Bachelor of Arts degree. Along with fellow Country singers Johnny Cash and Rita Coolidge (who later became his second wife) he attended an alumni weekend to receive an honorary doctorate. He then won a Rhodes Scholarship to study at Merton College at the University of Oxford where he also played rugby, boxed and began to write songs. Through his manager Larry Parnes (the man himself) he got a record deal singing under the name of Kris Carson. Not much happened then, but he left Oxford with a Bachelor of Philosophy degree in English literature. In 1961 he married his girlfriend Fran Mavia Beer.

He was commissioned by the US army and later became a captain and a trained helicopter pilot stationed in Germany where he formed a band before being assigned to teaching English literature at West Point. He left the army and headed for Nashville, where he met Johnny Cash for whom he wrote some songs, including ‘Sunday Mornin’ Comin’ Down’ which won Song of the Year at the 1970 Country Music Association Awards. Janis Joplin, Gordon Lightfoot and Jerry Lee Lewis all had hits with his ‘Me and Bobby McGee’, Joe Simon too with ‘Help Me Make It Through the Night’, while Patti Page, Peggy Lee and Kenny Rogers were all blessed with success from his songs.

Kristofferson performed solo and recorded his own albums and appeared at big music events such as the Isle of Wight Festival. Then he entered the film business. He first appeared in _The_ _Last Movie_ (1971), Dennis Hopper’s follow-up to _Easy Rider_. Next, he starred in _Cisco Pike_ (1972), playing a musician and drug dealer with Gene Hackman, followed by _Blume in_ _Love_ for Paul Mazursky with George Segal, and three films directed by Sam Peckinpah: _Pat Garrett and Billy the Kid_, with the latter role for Kris, _Bring Me the Head of Alfredo Garcia_, a Western with Kris as ‘the Biker’, and _Convoy_, a trucking action-comedy with Ali MacGraw and Ernest Borgnine. Michael Ritchie’s _Semi-Tough_ followed and Kris was particularly good opposite an Oscar-winning Ellen Burstyn in Martin Scorsese’s _Alice Doesn’t Live Here Anymore_.

Perhaps Kris Kristofferson will be best-remembered as an actor for _A Star Is_ _Born_ with Barbra Streisand, where he played a self-destructive rock star on the wane, while his singing protégé (Streisand) is heading for stardom. The film won an Academy Award for the song ‘Evergreen’, while Streisand, Kristofferson, the film, the score and ‘Evergreen’ all won Golden Globes. Kris made more films including Alan J. Pakula’s _Rollover_ with Jane Fonda, _The Last Days of Frank and Jesse_ _James_ with Cash and Kris in the title roles, _Flashpoint_ with Treat Williams, Alan Rudolph’s _Trouble in Mind_ with Keith Carradine, and John Sayles’ Oscar-nominated _Lone Star_, as well as Michael Cimino’s financially disastrous _Heaven’s Gate_, co-starring Christopher Walken, Jeff Bridges, John Hurt and Isabelle Huppert, which was voted one of the 100 greatest American films of all time by _BBC Culture_. His music and acting careers were in a state of flux but Kristofferson kept both going. There were good times such as working with Willie Nelson, Dolly Parton and Brenda Lee, and he and Nelson starred in Alan Rudolph’s _Songwriter_(1984) for which he was nominated for an Oscar for best original song score.

He continued to release albums and in 2009 the LP _Closer to the Bone_ found him in nostalgic mood reflecting on life as it is now. He received the honour of being Broadcast Music Inc’s Icon at the 2009 BMI Country Awards, just one of four dozen such accolades he had gathered over the years. He also won several Country Music Association Awards, including Lifetime Achievement, and he won four Grammys. His final concert was held in Fort Pierce, Florida, in 2020.

Kristofferson held differing political views but played benefits for the United Farm Workers, Palestinian children and for Leonard Peltier, a Native American activist wrongly accused of murder. Kris was a good man and performer but, according to one of his wives, he was a terrible husband. After his first marriage to Fran Mavia Beer ended in divorce in 1969, he married Rita Coolidge in 1973. After that divorce (in 1980) he wed Lisa Meyers. He had eight children from his three wives.

**MICHAEL DARVELL**

Trace Adkins costars in a new film that's sure to encourage viewers to follow their dreams and express themselves. The new movie, released March 16th in theaters, is called _I Can Only Imagine_, based on the popular Christian song of the same title.

The film follows MercyMe's Bart Millard (played by J. Michael Finley)as he pens a song about the complicated relationship he had with his dad who passed away when Bart was 18 years old. His father, Arthur, is played by Dennis Quaid. Trace Adkins takes on the role of another older male influence, Scott Brickell, MercyMe's manager since 2001.

**Read More:[See Kris Kristofferson and Trace Adkins Reunite for New Western Film 'Hickok'](https://www.wideopencountry.com/kris-kristofferson-trace-adkins-hickok)**

In the film's trailer, Adkins is briefly seen encouraging Finley's character to address the pain he feels when thinking about his father through music. Adkins' deep, gravely voice gives immediate depth to the character and weight to what he's suggesting. Though neither of them knows it at the time, the song he encourages the MercyMe singer to write eventually becomes one of the most popular Christian radio songs of all time.

MercyMe rerecorded "I Can Only Imagine" and released a new music video featuring clips of the film seen [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZNDEyxEMNp0). They also added a sweeping sound to the song, giving it a cinematic feel.
